nodes.title: Turn
nodes.description: One user message plus everything the agent does in response, up until it yields back to the user. Contains one or more provider requests.
nodes.body:
# Turn

> One user message plus everything the agent does in response, up until it yields back to the user. Contains one or more provider requests.

What makes the turn worth naming is that its length is the agent's decision, not yours. You hand over one message; the agent decides how many tool calls to chain before yielding. A turn can be a one-sentence answer or twenty minutes of reading, editing, and running tests. That's the same property from two angles: long turns are what make AFK work possible, and long turns are also where agents can drift off-course if unsteered.

Links: [agent](./agent.md), [model-provider-request](./model-provider-request.md), [tool](./tool.md), [session](./session.md), [afk](./afk.md), [harness](./harness.md), [tool-call](./tool-call.md), [tool-result](./tool-result.md), [model-provider](./model-provider.md), [stateful](./stateful.md)

nodes.title: Session
nodes.description: The unbroken conversational context and history accumulated between the user and the agent.
nodes.body:
# Session

> The unbroken conversational context and history accumulated between the user and the agent.

A session captures the complete lineage of prompts, system directives, tool invocations, and observations in a continuous stateful thread until compacted or reset.

Links: [turn](./turn.md), [harness](./harness.md), [context-window](./context-window.md), [compaction](./compaction.md), [stateful](./stateful.md)

nodes.title: Harness
nodes.description: The host software wrapping the raw model: executes tool calls, manages context windows, and maintains the loop.
nodes.body:
# Harness

> The host software wrapping the raw model: executes tool calls, manages context windows, and maintains the loop.

The harness is everything around the model: the parser that intercepts tool requests, executes shell/filesystem actions on the host machine, and feeds formatted results back into the next prompt.

Links: [agent](./agent.md), [tool](./tool.md), [turn](./turn.md), [session](./session.md), [environment](./environment.md), [sandboxing](./sandboxing.md)

nodes.title: Tool Call
nodes.description: A structured command generated by the model requesting the harness to execute a specific function.
nodes.body:
# Tool Call

> A structured command generated by the model requesting the harness to execute a specific function.

The model signals its intent by outputting arguments for a defined tool schema. The harness pauses model generation, executes the function, and injects the output as a Tool Result.

Links: [tool](./tool.md), [tool-result](./tool-result.md), [turn](./turn.md), [harness](./harness.md)

nodes.title: Tool Result
nodes.description: The actual output returned by the environment after executing a tool call, fed back into context.
nodes.body:
# Tool Result

> The actual output returned by the environment after executing a tool call, fed back into context.

Contains stdout, stderr, or structured payloads. Provides empirical feedback that allows the agent to self-correct and verify results before proceeding.

Links: [tool-call](./tool-call.md), [turn](./turn.md), [chain-of-thought](./chain-of-thought.md), [steering](./steering.md)

nodes.title: Model Provider Request
nodes.description: A single HTTP/gRPC invocation sending the context window to the LLM API and receiving tokens.
nodes.body:
# Model Provider Request

> A single HTTP/gRPC invocation sending the context window to the LLM API and receiving tokens.

Each turn consists of one or more discrete provider requests separated by tool executions. Provider latency, rate limits, and TTFT (time to first token) determine agent responsiveness.

Links: [model-provider](./model-provider.md), [turn](./turn.md), [input-tokens](./input-tokens.md), [output-tokens](./output-tokens.md), [inference](./inference.md)

nodes.title: Model Provider
nodes.description: The hosting platform (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, AWS Bedrock) serving LLM inference endpoints.
nodes.body:
# Model Provider

> The hosting platform (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, AWS Bedrock) serving LLM inference endpoints.

Provides API gateways, tokenizer engines, prompt caching infrastructure, and hardware accelerators (GPUs/TPUs).

Links: [model-provider-request](./model-provider-request.md), [prefix-cache](./prefix-cache.md), [inference](./inference.md), [model](./model.md)

nodes.title: Prefix Cache
nodes.description: Server-side key-value cache reusing computed activations across matching prompt prefixes.
nodes.body:
# Prefix Cache

> Server-side key-value cache reusing computed activations across matching prompt prefixes.

When the initial tokens of a prompt match a previously evaluated prompt (e.g. system instructions, tool schemas, file dumps), the provider skips re-evaluating the attention matrix.

Links: [cache-tokens](./cache-tokens.md), [input-tokens](./input-tokens.md), [model-provider](./model-provider.md), [system-prompt](./system-prompt.md)

nodes.title: Cache Tokens
nodes.description: Prompt tokens that hit precomputed KV-cache slots at the provider, billed at a steep discount.
nodes.body:
# Cache Tokens

> Prompt tokens that hit precomputed KV-cache slots at the provider, billed at a steep discount.

Drastically reduces both monetary cost (typically 10-25% of standard input price) and time-to-first-token during long agentic coding sessions.

Links: [prefix-cache](./prefix-cache.md), [input-tokens](./input-tokens.md), [output-tokens](./output-tokens.md)

nodes.title: Input Tokens
nodes.description: All text and tool results encoded into vocabulary IDs and passed into the model attention context.
nodes.body:
# Input Tokens

> All text and tool results encoded into vocabulary IDs and passed into the model attention context.

Input tokens scale linearly with context window depth and are processed in parallel across GPU matrix cores during the prefill phase.

Links: [output-tokens](./output-tokens.md), [cache-tokens](./cache-tokens.md), [context-window](./context-window.md)

nodes.title: Output Tokens
nodes.description: Newly generated tokens emitted autoregressively by the model during the decode phase.
nodes.body:
# Output Tokens

> Newly generated tokens emitted autoregressively by the model during the decode phase.

Generated sequentially (one token per forward pass). Bound by GPU memory bandwidth and generation latency, making output generation much slower than input processing.

Links: [input-tokens](./input-tokens.md), [turn](./turn.md), [sampling](./sampling.md)

nodes.title: Stateful Agent
nodes.description: An agent workflow maintaining working memory, scratchpads, and persistent disk state across turns.
nodes.body:
# Stateful Agent

> An agent workflow maintaining working memory, scratchpads, and persistent disk state across turns.

Unlike single-shot prompt completions, stateful agents inspect their own prior actions, maintain scratchpad plans, and navigate deep directory structures over time.

Links: [session](./session.md), [turn](./turn.md), [stateless](./stateless.md), [agent-memory](./agent-memory.md)

nodes.title: Stateless Model
nodes.description: The fundamental mathematical property of neural weights: zero memory between discrete forward passes.
nodes.body:
# Stateless Model

> The fundamental mathematical property of neural weights: zero memory between discrete forward passes.

Every API call starts completely blank. The model only knows what is explicitly present in the token stream of the current context window.

Links: [stateful](./stateful.md), [model](./model.md), [weights](./weights.md), [context-window](./context-window.md)

nodes.title: Context Compaction
nodes.description: Algorithmic summarization or pruning of older turn history to fit within context limits.
nodes.body:
# Context Compaction

> Algorithmic summarization or pruning of older turn history to fit within context limits.

When approaching context window limits, the harness invokes a summarizer pass that replaces detailed tool logs with a concise state digest.

Links: [session](./session.md), [context-window](./context-window.md), [attention-degradation](./attention-degradation.md)

nodes.title: Model
nodes.description: The parameters. Stateless — does next-token prediction and nothing else.
nodes.body:
# Model

> The parameters. Stateless — does next-token prediction and nothing else.

The core neural network weights trained on trillions of tokens. It takes a sequence of token IDs and computes a probability distribution over the next token in the vocabulary.

Links: [agent](./agent.md), [tool](./tool.md), [inference](./inference.md), [weights](./weights.md), [context-window](./context-window.md)

nodes.title: Agent
nodes.description: A model harnessed with tools, a system prompt, and an active context window loop.
nodes.body:

> A model harnessed with tools, a system prompt, and an active context window loop.

An autonomous system that combines a foundation model with tool schemas, memory, planning algorithms, and environmental feedback loops.

nodes.title: Tool
nodes.description: A function the harness exposes for the agent to call (e.g. read_file, edit_file, run_command).
nodes.body:
# Tool

> A function the harness exposes for the agent to call (e.g. read_file, edit_file, run_command).

The sensory and effector organs of an AI system. Defined via JSON schema with descriptions, parameter types, and strict contracts.

nodes.title: Inference
nodes.description: The execution phase where input tokens pass through transformer layers to produce logits.
nodes.body:
# Inference

> The execution phase where input tokens pass through transformer layers to produce logits.

Involves a prefill stage (evaluating all prompt tokens in parallel) followed by an autoregressive decode stage (sampling one token per step).

Links: [model](./model.md), [sampling](./sampling.md), [temperature](./temperature.md), [model-provider-request](./model-provider-request.md)

nodes.title: System Prompt
nodes.description: Top-level directives defining the persona, behavioral rules, constraints, and tool documentation.
nodes.body:
# System Prompt

> Top-level directives defining the persona, behavioral rules, constraints, and tool documentation.

Sets the tone, format guidelines, safety guardrails, and decision frameworks. Placed at the very top of the context window to maximize attention influence.

Links: [agent](./agent.md), [prefix-cache](./prefix-cache.md), [attention-degradation](./attention-degradation.md), [steering](./steering.md)

nodes.title: Context Window
nodes.description: The maximum token buffer size the model can attend to in a single forward pass.
nodes.body:
# Context Window

> The maximum token buffer size the model can attend to in a single forward pass.

Modern frontier models support 128k to 2M tokens. However, effective retrieval and instruction following can degrade across extremely long windows.

Links: [model](./model.md), [session](./session.md), [compaction](./compaction.md), [attention-degradation](./attention-degradation.md), [needle-in-a-haystack](./needle-in-a-haystack.md)

nodes.title: Temperature
nodes.description: Hyperparameter scaling the logit distribution before softmax sampling.
nodes.body:
# Temperature

> Hyperparameter scaling the logit distribution before softmax sampling.

A temperature of 0.0 forces greedy deterministic selection of the top logit, standard for code generation and mathematical reasoning. Higher values increase diversity.

Links: [sampling](./sampling.md), [inference](./inference.md), [model](./model.md)

nodes.title: Sampling Strategy
nodes.description: Algorithms (top-p nucleus, top-k, greedy) converting output logits into concrete tokens.
nodes.body:
# Sampling Strategy

> Algorithms (top-p nucleus, top-k, greedy) converting output logits into concrete tokens.

Determines how the model chooses from candidate next tokens based on probability mass thresholds.

Links: [temperature](./temperature.md), [inference](./inference.md), [output-tokens](./output-tokens.md)

nodes.title: Model Quantization
nodes.description: Compressing 16-bit floating point weights into 8-bit or 4-bit integer representations.
nodes.body:
# Model Quantization

> Compressing 16-bit floating point weights into 8-bit or 4-bit integer representations.

Techniques like AWQ, GPTQ, and GGUF allow local edge inference on Apple Silicon or consumer GPUs with minimal perplexity degradation.

Links: [weights](./weights.md), [model](./model.md), [inference](./inference.md)

nodes.title: Weights & Biases
nodes.description: The learned parameter tensors stored across transformer attention and MLP matrices.
nodes.body:
# Weights & Biases

> The learned parameter tensors stored across transformer attention and MLP matrices.

Billions of matrix weights fine-tuned during pretraining, RLHF, and DPO stages to encode programming patterns and human intent.

Links: [model](./model.md), [quantization](./quantization.md), [stateless](./stateless.md)

nodes.title: Execution Environment
nodes.description: The operating system container, sandbox, or virtual machine where tools run.
nodes.body:

Provides a bash shell, Node.js runtime, compilers, and network interfaces with strict security boundaries.

nodes.title: Bash Execution Tool
nodes.description: Tool enabling the agent to execute shell commands directly in the environment.
nodes.body:
# Bash Execution Tool

> Tool enabling the agent to execute shell commands directly in the environment.

Enables compiling projects, running tests, inspecting git logs, and installing packages. Usually paired with timeout limits and background task managers.

nodes.title: Virtual File System
nodes.description: The workspace directory tree accessed and modified by agent file tools.
nodes.body:
# Virtual File System

> The workspace directory tree accessed and modified by agent file tools.

Directly inspected via list_dir, view_file, and edited via surgical replacement chunks without overwriting full files blindly.

Links: [read-modify-write](./read-modify-write.md), [diff-tool](./diff-tool.md), [environment](./environment.md)

nodes.title: Surgical Diff / Edit Tool
nodes.description: Tool that applies precise string replacement chunks instead of rewriting entire files.
nodes.body:
# Surgical Diff / Edit Tool

> Tool that applies precise string replacement chunks instead of rewriting entire files.

Prevents accidental deletions of large existing files by matching exact unique TargetContent strings and substituting ReplacementContent.

Links: [file-system](./file-system.md), [read-modify-write](./read-modify-write.md), [anti-typo-rule](./anti-typo-rule.md)

nodes.title: Read-Modify-Write Protocol
nodes.description: Mandatory pattern: view_file must be called before editing any code to ensure exact match.
nodes.body:
# Read-Modify-Write Protocol

> Mandatory pattern: view_file must be called before editing any code to ensure exact match.

Eliminates "target content not found" errors and hallucinated file structures by enforcing live disk verification prior to diff generation.

Links: [diff-tool](./diff-tool.md), [file-system](./file-system.md), [anti-typo-rule](./anti-typo-rule.md)

nodes.title: Anti-Typo Path Rule
nodes.description: Strict validation preventing hallucinated whitespace, URL encodings (%20), or blended words in paths.
nodes.body:
# Anti-Typo Path Rule

> Strict validation preventing hallucinated whitespace, URL encodings (%20), or blended words in paths.

Verifies every path parameter against the live file tree before issuing create_file or edit_file calls.

Links: [file-system](./file-system.md), [read-modify-write](./read-modify-write.md), [diff-tool](./diff-tool.md)

nodes.title: Environment Sandboxing
nodes.description: Isolation layer (gVisor, Docker, Firecracker) restricting agent access to host systems.
nodes.body:
# Environment Sandboxing

> Isolation layer (gVisor, Docker, Firecracker) restricting agent access to host systems.

Prevents dangerous syscalls, isolates network routing, and limits CPU/RAM consumption during code execution.

Links: [environment](./environment.md), [bash-tool](./bash-tool.md), [harness](./harness.md)

nodes.title: Language Server Protocol (LSP)
nodes.description: Tool querying TypeScript/Rust compiler diagnostics, jump-to-definition, and symbol references.
nodes.body:
# Language Server Protocol (LSP)

> Tool querying TypeScript/Rust compiler diagnostics, jump-to-definition, and symbol references.

Feeds exact type errors, autocomplete signatures, and call hierarchies to the agent, dramatically reducing hallucinated API usage.

Links: [tool](./tool.md), [compile-check](./compile-check.md), [lint-verifier](./lint-verifier.md)

nodes.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
nodes.description: Open standard protocol connecting agents to external data sources, tools, and SaaS APIs.
nodes.body:
# Model Context Protocol (MCP)

> Open standard protocol connecting agents to external data sources, tools, and SaaS APIs.

Provides a standard JSON-RPC interface for clients (like Claude Desktop or AI Studio) to discover tools, prompts, and resources from MCP servers.

Links: [tool](./tool.md), [harness](./harness.md), [environment](./environment.md)

nodes.title: Subagent Delegation
nodes.description: Spawning specialized secondary agent instances to solve focused sub-problems in parallel.
nodes.body:
# Subagent Delegation

> Spawning specialized secondary agent instances to solve focused sub-problems in parallel.

The parent agent delegates a task (e.g. "write unit tests for auth module") to a fresh subagent, keeping the parent context clean and focused on high-level orchestration.

Links: [agent](./agent.md), [harness](./harness.md), [planning](./planning.md)

nodes.title: Away From Keyboard (AFK)
nodes.description: Long-running autonomous execution where the agent works independently without human intervention.
nodes.body:
# Away From Keyboard (AFK)

> Long-running autonomous execution where the agent works independently without human intervention.

The hallmark of high-agency coding agents. Capable of planning, executing tens of tool calls, fixing test failures, and delivering working PRs while the developer is asleep or in meetings.

Links: [turn](./turn.md), [steering](./steering.md), [agent](./agent.md), [autonomous-execution](./autonomous-execution.md), [planning](./planning.md)

nodes.title: Human Steering & Course Correction
nodes.description: Mid-flight guidance providing feedback or altering direction when an agent begins to drift.
nodes.body:
# Human Steering & Course Correction

> Mid-flight guidance providing feedback or altering direction when an agent begins to drift.

A short prompt ("Focus on fixing the login bug first before refactoring styles") that re-anchors attention and prevents rabbit holes.

Links: [afk](./afk.md), [agent](./agent.md), [human-in-the-loop](./human-in-the-loop.md), [planning](./planning.md)

nodes.title: Chain-of-Thought (CoT)
nodes.description: Step-by-step internal reasoning traces emitted before taking external tool actions.
nodes.body:
# Chain-of-Thought (CoT)

> Step-by-step internal reasoning traces emitted before taking external tool actions.

Allows the model to decompose complex problems, explore alternative hypotheses, and check edge cases before outputting tool arguments.

Links: [reasoning-effort](./reasoning-effort.md), [planning](./planning.md), [backtracking](./backtracking.md)

nodes.title: Reasoning Effort & Thinking Budget
nodes.description: Configurable parameter (low, medium, high) allocating hidden thinking tokens for deep analysis.
nodes.body:
# Reasoning Effort & Thinking Budget

> Configurable parameter (low, medium, high) allocating hidden thinking tokens for deep analysis.

Higher reasoning effort allows models like Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking or Claude 3.7 Sonnet Thinking to evaluate dozens of hypothesis branches before generating code.

Links: [chain-of-thought](./chain-of-thought.md), [planning](./planning.md), [model](./model.md)

nodes.title: Multi-Step Planning
nodes.description: Creating structured checklists and roadmaps before implementing multi-file changes.
nodes.body:
# Multi-Step Planning

> Creating structured checklists and roadmaps before implementing multi-file changes.

Prevents erratic trial-and-error by establishing a clear definition of done, verifying prerequisites, and executing changes in logical dependency order.

Links: [chain-of-thought](./chain-of-thought.md), [backtracking](./backtracking.md), [afk](./afk.md), [steering](./steering.md)

nodes.title: Algorithmic Backtracking
nodes.description: Recognizing a failed approach, reverting bad edits, and attempting an alternative strategy.
nodes.body:
# Algorithmic Backtracking

> Recognizing a failed approach, reverting bad edits, and attempting an alternative strategy.

A key indicator of advanced agents: instead of doubling down on broken code, the agent uses git checkout to revert and tries an entirely different architectural path.

Links: [planning](./planning.md), [chain-of-thought](./chain-of-thought.md), [compile-check](./compile-check.md)

nodes.title: Autonomous Execution
nodes.description: The ability of an agent to chain tools, evaluate outputs, and reach a goal without prompts.
nodes.body:
# Autonomous Execution

> The ability of an agent to chain tools, evaluate outputs, and reach a goal without prompts.

Combines perception, reasoning, and environmental manipulation into an unbroken cycle until acceptance criteria are satisfied.

Links: [afk](./afk.md), [agent](./agent.md), [harness](./harness.md), [turn](./turn.md)

nodes.title: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)
nodes.description: Architectural pattern requiring explicit human approval before executing sensitive operations.
nodes.body:
# Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)

> Architectural pattern requiring explicit human approval before executing sensitive operations.

Used for high-risk operations like database drops, payment setups, OAuth credential granting, or committing to main.

Links: [steering](./steering.md), [sandboxing](./sandboxing.md), [agent](./agent.md)

nodes.title: Empirical Grounding
nodes.description: Anchoring agent decisions in real runtime output (compilers, linters, tests) rather than guesses.
nodes.body:
# Empirical Grounding

> Anchoring agent decisions in real runtime output (compilers, linters, tests) rather than guesses.

Dramatically cuts hallucinations by ensuring every code modification is validated through actual compiler diagnostics and test suites.

Links: [compile-check](./compile-check.md), [lint-verifier](./lint-verifier.md), [tool-result](./tool-result.md)

nodes.title: Attention Degradation
nodes.description: The loss of reasoning quality and instruction recall as context window length expands.
nodes.body:
# Attention Degradation

> The loss of reasoning quality and instruction recall as context window length expands.

Attention matrices dilute information over long horizons. Models are more likely to miss constraints placed in the middle of a 200k token context than in a lean 10k token prompt.

Links: [lost-in-the-middle](./lost-in-the-middle.md), [needle-in-a-haystack](./needle-in-a-haystack.md), [context-window](./context-window.md), [compaction](./compaction.md)

nodes.title: Hallucination
nodes.description: Plausible-sounding but factually false outputs, non-existent packages, or fabricated APIs.
nodes.body:
# Hallucination

> Plausible-sounding but factually false outputs, non-existent packages, or fabricated APIs.

Occurs when probabilistic next-token generation favors fluent patterns over factual truth. Mitigated through empirical grounding, tool use, and strict system instructions.

Links: [grounding](./grounding.md), [anti-typo-rule](./anti-typo-rule.md), [attention-degradation](./attention-degradation.md)

nodes.title: Lost in the Middle Effect
nodes.description: Empirical finding that LLMs recall information at the start and end of prompts far better than the middle.
nodes.body:
# Lost in the Middle Effect

> Empirical finding that LLMs recall information at the start and end of prompts far better than the middle.

Attention mechanisms naturally focus on the prompt beginning (system instructions) and ending (latest user query). Critical constraints should be placed at these boundary positions.

Links: [attention-degradation](./attention-degradation.md), [needle-in-a-haystack](./needle-in-a-haystack.md), [context-window](./context-window.md)

nodes.title: Needle in a Haystack (NIAH)
nodes.description: Benchmark testing whether an LLM can retrieve a single isolated fact hidden within a massive document.
nodes.body:
# Needle in a Haystack (NIAH)

> Benchmark testing whether an LLM can retrieve a single isolated fact hidden within a massive document.

Tests factual retrieval across different context depths (10k to 2M tokens) and document positions (0% to 100%).

Links: [context-window](./context-window.md), [lost-in-the-middle](./lost-in-the-middle.md), [attention-degradation](./attention-degradation.md)

nodes.title: Progressive Disclosure
nodes.description: Providing minimal high-level context first, letting the agent fetch deeper details via tools on demand.
nodes.body:
# Progressive Disclosure

> Providing minimal high-level context first, letting the agent fetch deeper details via tools on demand.

Instead of dumping all 500 files into context, provide an outline or file tree and allow the agent to view_file only what it needs. Keeps context clean and fast.

Links: [context-window](./context-window.md), [prefix-cache](./prefix-cache.md), [attention-degradation](./attention-degradation.md)

nodes.title: System Prompt Cache Alignment
nodes.description: Designing system prompts with static prefixes to maximize 100% cache hits across all turns.
nodes.body:
# System Prompt Cache Alignment

> Designing system prompts with static prefixes to maximize 100% cache hits across all turns.

Placing static rules at the very top and dynamic user queries at the bottom ensures the entire system prompt and tool definitions hit the KV-cache.

Links: [prefix-cache](./prefix-cache.md), [system-prompt](./system-prompt.md), [cache-tokens](./cache-tokens.md)

nodes.title: Few-Shot Exemplars
nodes.description: Providing 2-3 concrete input/output examples within the prompt to enforce exact syntax contracts.
nodes.body:
# Few-Shot Exemplars

> Providing 2-3 concrete input/output examples within the prompt to enforce exact syntax contracts.

Far more effective than abstract prose rules. Showing the model exact JSON payloads or diff formats prevents formatting errors.

Links: [system-prompt](./system-prompt.md), [grounding](./grounding.md)

nodes.title: Evals & Benchmarking
nodes.description: Systematic measurement of model accuracy, tool execution speed, token efficiency, and reasoning depth.
nodes.body:
# Evals & Benchmarking

> Systematic measurement of model accuracy, tool execution speed, token efficiency, and reasoning depth.

Standardizes measurement across diverse coding tasks to track regressions, latency improvements, and model upgrades.

Links: [swe-bench](./swe-bench.md), [pass-at-1](./pass-at-1.md), [golden-dataset](./golden-dataset.md)

nodes.title: Canary Test
nodes.description: A hidden probe test embedded in codebases to detect data contamination and benchmark memorization.
nodes.body:
# Canary Test

> A hidden probe test embedded in codebases to detect data contamination and benchmark memorization.

Ensures high benchmark scores reflect true generalized reasoning rather than pretraining data leakage.

Links: [golden-dataset](./golden-dataset.md), [benchmark](./benchmark.md)

nodes.title: Test-Driven Agent (TDD Loop)
nodes.description: Agent workflow that writes failing unit tests first, implements code, and iterates until all pass.
nodes.body:
# Test-Driven Agent (TDD Loop)

> Agent workflow that writes failing unit tests first, implements code, and iterates until all pass.

Creates a deterministic acceptance contract. The agent writes a test replicating a bug, verifies it fails, edits the source, and stops only when the test is green.

Links: [grounding](./grounding.md), [compile-check](./compile-check.md), [backtracking](./backtracking.md)

nodes.title: Graph RAG
nodes.description: Retrieval Augmented Generation traversing structured entity graphs rather than raw text chunks.
nodes.body:
# Graph RAG

> Retrieval Augmented Generation traversing structured entity graphs rather than raw text chunks.

Extracts entity relationships and community clusters from codebases (ASTs, call graphs) to feed coherent dependency subgraphs into the prompt.

Links: [semantic-embeddings](./semantic-embeddings.md), [ast-graph](./ast-graph.md), [dependency-graph](./dependency-graph.md), [agent-memory](./agent-memory.md)

nodes.title: Semantic Embeddings
nodes.description: Dense vector representations mapping code and text into continuous semantic similarity space.
nodes.body:
# Semantic Embeddings

> Dense vector representations mapping code and text into continuous semantic similarity space.

Generated by embedding models (e.g. text-embedding-3) to power approximate nearest neighbor searches over large documentation libraries.

Links: [vector-database](./vector-database.md), [graph-rag](./graph-rag.md)

nodes.title: Vector Database
nodes.description: Specialized database index (HNSW, IVF) querying millions of high-dimensional vectors in milliseconds.
nodes.body:
# Vector Database

> Specialized database index (HNSW, IVF) querying millions of high-dimensional vectors in milliseconds.

Stores codebase embeddings and metadata, allowing agents to retrieve relevant snippets for any natural language query.

Links: [semantic-embeddings](./semantic-embeddings.md), [graph-rag](./graph-rag.md)

nodes.title: Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)
nodes.description: Tree representation of source code structure used for precise symbol navigation and refactoring.
nodes.body:
# Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)

> Tree representation of source code structure used for precise symbol navigation and refactoring.

Parsed via tools like tree-sitter. Allows agents to extract function signatures, scope boundaries, and call sites with 100% syntactic precision.

Links: [dependency-graph](./dependency-graph.md), [graph-rag](./graph-rag.md), [lsp-tool](./lsp-tool.md)

nodes.title: Dependency Graph
nodes.description: Directed graph capturing import/export relationships and call hierarchies across all modules.
nodes.body:
# Dependency Graph

> Directed graph capturing import/export relationships and call hierarchies across all modules.

Maps which files import a component, preventing breaking changes by revealing all downstream consumers before applying an edit.

Links: [ast-graph](./ast-graph.md), [graph-rag](./graph-rag.md), [read-modify-write](./read-modify-write.md)

nodes.title: Knowledge Triplestore
nodes.description: Graph database storing facts as (Subject, Predicate, Object) triples queryable via formal logic.
nodes.body:
# Knowledge Triplestore

> Graph database storing facts as (Subject, Predicate, Object) triples queryable via formal logic.

Represents code relations (e.g. Button Component, Renders, Icon) allowing deterministic graph traversal and SPARQL queries.

Links: [graph-rag](./graph-rag.md), [semantic-embeddings](./semantic-embeddings.md)

nodes.title: Long-Term Agent Memory
nodes.description: Persistent key-value and graph storage retaining user preferences, project conventions, and past learnings.
nodes.body:
# Long-Term Agent Memory

> Persistent key-value and graph storage retaining user preferences, project conventions, and past learnings.

Stored in files like AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, or vector memories. Automatically loaded by the harness into the system prompt across future sessions.

Links: [stateful](./stateful.md), [session](./session.md), [system-prompt](./system-prompt.md), [graph-rag](./graph-rag.md)
